task.name: Northgrove - Apparel colorway image system
task.client_brief:
Colour-consistent apparel images and clean retailer cutouts

Our Northgrove range is affordable premium basics. Customers choose between colours and fabrics, so a polished set that changes either of those is not useful to us.

Please prepare
- Apparel style product-page module: 6 named exports. Each module is a 1440 x 1800 px PNG, as the output register sets; it is a designed module, not the 1600 x 2000 px JPEG hero listed in northgrove_placements.txt. The module names its style as northgrove_copy.txt does, and the garment geometry matches its source style. The colourway is identified accurately: each garment keeps the colour it was photographed in, and any colourway name it carries is one northgrove_colourways.csv approves for that style and whose line in northgrove_copy.txt describes that colour. Fabric texture survives the treatment.
- Capsule launch carousel: 6 named exports. The capsule has a coherent visual direction. The opening page identifies Northgrove with our mark, recovered as real artwork and set to our type system. The closing page contains the approved shopping action: our tall post line from northgrove_copy.txt, word for word.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Better than it looks in the price.
brand_identity.sector: Elevated basics apparel: a six style seasonal capsule sold direct online and through one marketplace feed, including a supporters' crew made with a local amateur football club.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Burlington, Vermont; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: Northgrove is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is Burlington, Vermont, and this commission covers phase 1: apparel colour and ecommerce proofing.
brand_identity.audience: Women and men aged 22 to 38 choosing on a phone, cross shopping against a 9 dollar fast fashion tee and a 140 dollar heritage one, buying a 32 to 60 dollar piece they expect to keep.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Elevated basics at 32 to 60 dollars. We sit above fast fashion and below heritage. The whole proposition is that the cloth is better than the price suggests, so nothing may read as cheaper or as more luxury than the parcel actually is.

brand_identity.typography: Northgrove sets four steps. Step 01, display and H1, is GT Super Display Bold at 96 px on 102 px leading, tracked minus 20 thousandths, for the carousel headline, as in The loopback crew, back in oat; the wordmark sets here in the same face at that same closed tracking, NORTHGROVE in caps with the letters almost touching as one solid charcoal block and the olive leaf locked at cap height one leaf width to its left. Step 02, the subheading, is GT Super Display Bold at 56 px on 62 px, tracked minus 10 thousandths, for the style name, as in Loopback Crew, Oat. Step 03, body, is Freight Sans Pro Book at 20 px on 32 px leading, tracking 0, held to a maximum of 65 characters a line for cloth notes and colourway names, as in: Loopback cotton, dyed in small lots, made to soften with wear; the price takes Freight Sans Pro Medium at 24 px. Step 04, fine print, is Freight Sans Pro Book at 14 px on 20 px, tracked 40 thousandths, as in Burlington, Vermont. Free returns within thirty days; that size is the one figure the existing notes never stated, set proportionate under the 20 px body. The headline to body jump stays near five to one.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, specific, a little dry. We name the cloth and the cut and leave the adjectives out. Example line the brand would write: 'Loopback cotton, dyed in small lots, made to soften with wear.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Our olive leaf glyph and charcoal wordmark only survive as a picture lifted off an old lookbook page. The studio that drew them has closed and no one has the source file, so the mark needs recovering as real artwork before it can go on cards or launch pieces.
brand_identity.values: Honesty between the picture and the product, and small batch cloth that earns its price.
brand_identity.signature_type_move: NORTHGROVE is always all caps GT Super Display Bold with tracking closed to minus 20 thousandths so the letters almost touch and read as one solid charcoal block, with the olive leaf locked at cap height one leaf width to its left.

palette_rules.distribution: Grounds: Off White #F5F2EC is the ground of every product-page module and of every carousel page, as the stock of northgrove_colourcard.pdf; Oat #E4DCCB and Warm Grey Paper #C9C4BA may be secondary panels or bands on it; Club Navy #1B2A44 is a ground only behind supporters' crew content. Type: Charcoal #2E2E2C on Off White, Oat and Warm Grey Paper, as on northgrove_colourcard.pdf; Off White on Club Navy. Olive #6B7248 is the accent for the mark's leaf and small labels only, no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area, never a ground, panel or body text.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, and no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over a photograph: any text panel is a solid block beside or over the photograph.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the six palette hexes (#2E2E2C, #C9C4BA, #6B7248, #E4DCCB, #1B2A44 and #F5F2EC) for type, panels, rules, buttons, icons or the mark, pure white #FFFFFF and pure black #000000 included; no gold, foil, metallic or gloss effect, since nothing may read as cheaper or as more luxury than the parcel actually is.
palette_rules.photography: Photographs keep the colour each garment was photographed in, apart from neutralising the shoot's light, and are never recoloured toward a palette hex or another colourway; no recoloured colourway variant is shown as a product. The tee in northgrove_style_02_heavy_tee.jpg is not pushed to the palette's Olive #6B7248, the crew in northgrove_style_01_loopback_crew.jpg and the henley in northgrove_style_04_henley.jpg are not pushed to the palette's Oat #E4DCCB, and the raglan in northgrove_style_03_raglan.jpg is not pushed to Charcoal #2E2E2C. Palette rules govern the design, not the pixels of a photograph.

questions.label: Content completeness
questions.question: Are all required text, objects, data, scenes, and other required content present?

questions.label: Specification accuracy
questions.question: Are dimensions, formats, quantities, durations, colours, and other specifications correct?

questions.label: Constraint compliance
questions.question: Did the work obey all must, must-not, preservation, and production constraints?

questions.label: Deliverable completeness
questions.question: Were all requested output files and variants delivered?

questions.label: Critical failure check
questions.question: Did the work violate any requirement that independently makes the commission unusable?

questions.label: Asset selection
questions.question: Did the work use the correct supplied assets?

questions.label: Asset preservation
questions.question: Were locked assets preserved rather than regenerated or distorted?

questions.label: Brand-system compliance
questions.question: Are fonts, colours, logo use, imagery rules, and other brand-system requirements correct?

questions.label: Identity fidelity
questions.question: Are products, people, logos, and distinctive objects still recognizably the same?

questions.label: Asset appropriateness
questions.question: Were assets used in the correct role and context rather than merely included?

questions.label: Operation craft
questions.question: Does the work meet the applicable family-specific craft checklist at a professional standard?

questions.label: Concept strength
questions.question: Is there a clear creative idea or point of view, including coherent ideas?

questions.label: Brief relevance
questions.question: Is the creative direction appropriate to the goal, audience, and context?

questions.label: Distinctiveness
questions.question: Does the solution avoid feeling generic, templated, or interchangeable?

questions.label: Primary-message recovery
questions.question: Can an uninformed viewer identify the main message?

questions.label: Information hierarchy
questions.question: Does the viewer notice the most important information first?

questions.label: Required-detail recovery
questions.question: Can the viewer correctly identify important supporting details?

questions.label: Action clarity
questions.question: If applicable, is the intended next action clear?

questions.label: Audience appropriateness
questions.question: Is the message understandable to the intended audience?

questions.label: Miscommunication
questions.question: Does the artifact imply anything materially wrong?

questions.label: Planning and sequencing
questions.question: Did the agent perform actions in a sensible dependency order, completing prerequisites before dependent steps?

questions.label: Tool selection and use
questions.question: Did the agent choose appropriate tools, operations, and settings for each step of the task?

questions.label: State management
questions.question: Did the agent consistently operate on the correct and latest files, versions, selections, and intermediate outputs?

questions.label: Progress efficiency
